title: The Fog That Stole the Song
markdown:
The sun burst over the harbour in oranges and pinks. Lyra bounced out of her seashell-dotted bed. Holiday. Their annual performance. The biggest splash of the season. A peculiar quiet had settled anyway. Seagulls sounded like whispers. Waves tapped the docks with a tired sigh.

Her bright blue tunic vibrated. Dark curls bounced as she dashed to the window. Below, Dock flipped and dived, but even his happy barks seemed flat. A flutter started in her tummy. “Dock! Ready for the big day?”

He zipped up, shaking diamond droplets from dark fur. “Ready as I’ll ever be.” His voice sounded muffled, as if he were speaking through a giant marshmallow. A seagull no bigger than Lyra’s hand fluttered down, glum. Its cries were dry leaves. “Lyra. Dock. A fog. A thick peculiar fog has swallowed our voices. The crabs can’t belt their shanties. The dolphins can’t whistle. Even the waves are murmurs.”

Lyra’s excitement dissolved. A fog that stole voices was no ordinary mist. Dock nudged her with a wet nose, eyes wide. “The performance. No music means no joy.” He paddled faster. “Maybe we wait. Maybe it blows away.”

She could not stand a silent world. Music chased shadows. “We can’t just wait. If the music is gone, we find it.” She tied her boots with a decisive knot. “Adventure is calling, and it sounds like it needs a song.”

She hopped into her zippy yellow skiff, enchanted to hum a jaunty tune that the fog immediately tried to sit on. Dock took the water, a dark torpedo of seal-shaped bravery, keeping his head up so he could watch her hands on the tiller. They left the holiday bunting looking limp. The muffling fog thickened, damp and heavy. The world dissolved into a hazy grey canvas. Sounds vanished before they arrived. It felt like being wrapped in a silent, damp, claustrophobic blanket. Lyra’s humming faltered and she let it. Forcing a tune here would only feed the grey.

“I can barely hear you,” Dock grumbled, paddling closer.

A grumpy crab scuttled out, pincers waving. “Can’t hear a blessed thing. Can’t sing without swallowing sand.” Lyra played a few bright lute notes. The fog gobbled them, leaving a faint melancholic echo. The crab shook its claws and vanished, muttering about the good old days.

“The music can’t break free.” The fog did not feel angry. It felt sad. They pressed on, Dock’s sense of direction their compass. Around wave-worn rocks the grey thinned. A hidden cove. On glistening kelp, a creature shimmered with faint light. An ancient sea spirit. Terribly lonely.

“She’s not being mean,” Lyra breathed. “She’s just sad.” Long ago the spirit had sung forgotten melodies that filled the ocean with magic. The world had moved on. Loneliness had swirled into this silencing fog.

Not a problem to conquer. A broken heart that wanted a melody. Lyra settled, fingers over the lute. She would not blast the fog. She would sing the spirit’s own forgotten tunes back to her, remembrance and comfort. Soft notes, first drop of dew. She hummed the deep resonant songs she imagined the ancient ocean had held, weaving them with her own. The fog clung. Despair arrived, cold and heavy. What if silence stayed?

Dock nudged her toward the water, firm, comforting. He could not conjure music. He understood when hers was most potent.

She sang again, not with force but with warmth. Joy the spirit’s music used to bring: dolphins’ leaps, crabs’ booming shanties, seagulls’ cries. A tapestry of forgotten melodies and harbour noise. The spirit’s shimmer grew. A single crystal tear rolled down and splashed. The fog receded with a contented sigh, not a rush.

Grey dissolved like a forgotten dream. Sparkling blue. Bustling colour. The crabs immediately launched into a boisterous tune. Seagulls cawed with delight. Waves crashed with renewed vigour. The tiny glum seagull found a proper shriek and used it at once.

Lyra and Dock, relief making them sloppy, raced back to the docks. The harbour pulsed. Music spilled everywhere, a joyous cacophony. The annual performance was about to begin, the atmosphere crackling. Lyra grinned at Dock, eyes shining. He barked, triumphant, and shook one last diamond spray over her boots on purpose. They did not need to announce that today would be amazing. The first note of the show did that for them, and the sea spirit, if anyone had looked back at the cove, was no longer quite so alone.
characters: Lyra (a music mage), Dock (a harbour seal)
